notes.claim: Third and other triple harmonic currents of a three-phase load are additive in the neutral and give additional heating of the cables, while the fundamentals of a balanced load cancel there.
Loads such as rectifiers, variable-speed drives and fluorescent lighting banks draw non-sinusoidal currents, so current can appear in the neutral where a balanced motor load would have none.

The neutral current can reach about 173% of phase current in a balanced system with these pulses, and one paper puts triplen neutral current at up to 3 times the phase fundamental, depending on how the percentage is referred.
The slides take the neutral current as Ibn = 3 × h × IL (3 × 0.35 × 150 = 157.5 A at 35%), which exceeds the 150 A line current, so Ibn becomes Ib.
The Table 4Aa bands in the slides: line current governs with factor 0.86 for 15 to 33% third harmonic, and above 33% the factor is applied to a calculated neutral current, not the line current.
Harmonics are only considered when the manufacturer's data says one is present; with no neutral conductor there can be no current in it.
The slides' worked example uses It ≥ 160 / (0.94 × 0.65 × 0.86) with the harmonic rating factor included in the divisor.
